sources.citation: Meader, Robert E. 1978. Índios do Nordeste: Levantamento sobre os remanescentes tribais do nordeste brasileiro (Série Lingüística 8). Brasília/Cuiabá: Summer Institute of Linguistics. Section 3.5 'Pankarú (Pankararú). Lista 1' (informant João Moreno, c. 50, Brejo dos Padres PE; investigator Wilbur Pickering, 1961), pp. 41-43 of the 1978 print (pp. 24-26 of the SIL reformatted PDF).
sources.note: Nothing as a rule. The only Pankararú material is an ~80-item phonetic wordlist (Parte A/B) transcribed with a stress mark ' and pitch/tone diacritics (e.g. 'žúbʌ̀ 'amarelo', 'tíŋgʌ́ 'branco', 'po 'fogo', 'žasì 'lua', 'ářà 'dia' vs. à'lų́ 'joelho', pəřə'nà 'mar', žá'gwà 'onça', pi'tų̀ 'noite', mʌ̨̀n'dī 'mandioca', sé'tį̀ 'meu nariz'); stress falls on different syllables in different items and no transcription key or comment on accent is given anywhere in the book. Introduction notes 26 of 80 items (32%) look Tupi and warns (Landerman note 2, p. 59) that the informants may have been giving Tup…

sources.citation: Arruti, José Maurício (IFCH, Unicamp) & Lilian Abram dos Santos (IEL, Unicamp). 2025. Parceria Universidade e escola: a retomada da Língua Pankararu. Projeto de pesquisa e extensão (Extecult, Unicamp; cadastrado 18/07/2025, deliberação 2025-12-05; contrapartida ao projeto FAPESP 2023/10271-3). Project description published on the Étnico blog, 15 Dec 2025.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. Its Justificativa states the documentary situation outright: 'Não há registro documental da ou das línguas faladas entre os habitantes do aldeamento do Brejo dos Padres.. É pouco provável que nesse nucleamento multiétnico tenha existido uma língua dominante além do português' (citing Arruti 1996, 1999), and that the surviving repertoire of ritual names, songs and toponyms 'já foram coletados em dois momentos, nos anos de 1930 e nos anos de 1960. Em ambos os casos, os linguistas responsáveis não puderam produzir juízo seguro sobre o tronco linguístico.. Kariri, Jê e…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page pank1250 (refs: Fabre 2005; Ethnologue 2025 status 'Dormant'); Wikipedia (en) 'Pankararú language' and (pt) 'Língua pancararu' (raw wikitext saved).
sources.note: Glottolog lists zero descriptive references. Wikipedia only reproduces the four wordlists (Nimuendajú 1935 'Macarú' ~20 words; Pompeu 1958; Carneiro in Loukotka 1963; Meader 1978) and says nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle. 2024. Unclassified and Spurious Languages. Chapter 5 of: The Indigenous Languages of the Americas: History and Classification, pp. 280-338. New York: Oxford University Press. DOI 10.1093/oso/9780197673461.003.0005.
sources.note: several short wordlists, scantly attested; Loukotka 1963's sixteen words are Kambiwa; no statement: nothing on stress, accent or tone anywhere in the chapter (the words stress/accent/tone/pitch/syllable do not occur); entry concerns attestation and classification only

sources.citation: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA). Povos Indigenas no Brasil (online encyclopedia), people entries 'Pankararu', 'Xakriaba', 'Arapaso' (M. Bonome Pederneiras, 2019 photo credit), 'Tora', 'Turiwara' (stub, 01/2014). pib.socioambiental.org, read 2026-09-21.
sources.note: Only sociolinguistic/ritual remarks (a 1990s press report of Pankararu in Sao Paulo 'conversando em sua lingua nativa, o Iate'; rezas 'na lingua dos antigos'); no linguistic data, nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Oliveira, Luís Antônio de. 2016. A língua Pankararu: puxando os fios da história. Percurso acadêmico (trabalho de conclusão, Licenciatura em Línguas, Artes e Literaturas), Formação Intercultural para Educadores Indígenas, Faculdade de Educação, Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (orient. Maria Gorete Neto). Belo Horizonte. 50 pp.
sources.note: No phonology content. A language-history / revitalization essay: land invasion and language loss, interview with the last rememberer Antônio Moreno (pp. 37-39: jaci, guaraci, katiti, kairé, marubixaba, adedui/adêduá 'menino/menina', kuiã 'mulher'), interviews with Museu-Escola Pankararu teachers, and school word tables (pp. 42-45: phrases 'Sé takui i gasú', word list Catu, Ará, Caruca, Pitunã, Rarietá, Porangá, Mokinkyá, numerals 0-10 Guáte he-é-dé, Céne, Dúni, Cúmu, Rékai, Tôerá.., animals Beró, Iaká, Buzucú, Kikó, Bukó, Itolokía, Fikia, Soá, Zagwa, Fitsaká, Iandirá..). Items carry Portugues…

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005 [rev. 2007]. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: entry PANKARARU / PANKARARÉ (3 pp.).
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; classification note (isolate; Greenberg's Macro-Tucanoan grouping on 5 supposed cognates), population, and a 50-item bibliography that is almost entirely ethnographic. Only linguistic-looking items: Meader 1978, Pompeu 1958, Loukotka 1963, Souza 1993 (Terra Indígena).

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 2000 [1935]. Cartas do sertão de Curt Nimuendajú para Carlos Estevão de Oliveira. Lisboa: Museu Nacional de Etnologia / Assírio & Alvim (letter of 16 March 1935 with ~20 'Macarú' words).
sources.note: Published version of Nimuendajú's Macarú/Pankararú words with Portuguese-style accents; could confirm stress marking on individual items. Open PDF on the Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú, not downloaded (large; low expected yield).

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 2000 [ms. 1935]. Cartas do Sertão de Curt Nimuendajú para Carlos Estevão de Oliveira (apresentação e notas Thekla Hartmann). Lisboa: Museu Nacional de Etnologia / Assírio & Alvim. Fig. 10, p. 13: 'Vocabulários comparados. Belém, 16.3.1935' (facsimile of a one-page typescript signed Curt Nimuendajú: Macarú | Šukurú | Fulnió | Karirí).
sources.note: Nothing stated. A 16-item typescript list with item-level accent marks (acute mostly on the final syllable: tuká, foiá, arraó, ginicaçí, canarí, tiaparú, sará, praiá; circumflex in sansê, matinadô, fenêkia; none on likim, poi, aleal, pucheren, tonan), no key, no comment; the published letters themselves (text searched for Macarú/Makurá/Pankararú/Brejo dos Padres/Tacaratu) contain no word list and no linguistic remark on this language beyond the 1937 and 1940 mentions of Estevão's visits.

sources.citation: Rodrigues, Aryon Dall'Igna. 1986. Línguas brasileiras: para o conhecimento das línguas indígenas. São Paulo: Edições Loyola. 134 pp.
sources.note: Named only among north-eastern peoples who 'falam, hoje, exclusivamente variedades regionais da língua portuguesa'; no language data, nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Silva, Orlando Sampaio. 1978. A última dimensão indígena dos Pankararu de Itaparica, Pernambuco. Anais do Museu de Antropologia da UFSC (Florianópolis) ano X, no. 11: 101-123. (Section 3.2 'Língua'.)
sources.note: Nothing on the sound system; the language section (3.2) only documents complete shift to Portuguese by the 1970s and reviews the affiliation debate (Pinto 1952: Jê; Estevão 1943: not predominantly Tupi; Ribeiro 1957: unclassified; Melatti 1972: 'grupos que deixaram de falar língua indígena'). Useful as a dated last-speaker record, not as a description.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center (Pankararú entry, pp. 87-88 per Meader 1978 n. 2).
sources.note: Compiles the pre-1961 Pankararú items (sol panyé, homem porkiá..) used by later classifiers; no stress statement expected, but it is the reference Glottolog-era surveys cite.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1963. Documents et vocabulaires inédits de langues et de dialectes sud-américains. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 52(1): 7-60 (Pankarurú words from the Raimundo Dantas Carneiro manuscript).
sources.note: Primary wordlist not yet opened; check Loukotka's remarks on the source and whether accent is marked. Open access on Persée but the PDF download is gated by an altcha challenge by automated download.

sources.citation: Hohenthal Jr., William D. 1960. As tribos indígenas do médio e baixo São Francisco. Revista do Museu Paulista, Nova Série XII: 37-71; followed by 'The general characteristics of Indian cultures in the Rio São Francisco valley', pp. 73-86 (the item Glottolog lists for pank1250). São Paulo.
sources.note: Nothing. The Pankararú entry is 18th-19th-century mission history (Ilha da Vargem, N. S. de Belém, N. S. do Ó; Brejo-dos-Padres founded c. 1802, 580 Indians in 1855, 290 in 1861, aldeia abolished 1875, SPI post 'Pancarús'); the English essay treats the valley's cultures generically and notes (p. 82) that only the Fulniô keep a living language. No word list, no phonetic remark; a full-text search for stress/accent acento/accent/stress/tônica returns nothing in the 57-page PDF.

sources.citation: Pinto, Estevão. 1958. Dados históricos e etnológicos sôbre os Pancararu de Tacaratu (remanescentes indígenas dos sertões de Pernambuco). In: Muxarabis & balcões e outros ensaios, 33-58 (notas 57-58). São Paulo: Companhia Editora Nacional (Brasiliana, vol. 303). Contains Cildo Meireles's c. 1915-1935 list of Pankararu ritual terms and toponyms (p. 35) with Pinto's comments (p. 36).
sources.note: An ethnographic-historical chapter; its only phonetic remark is the one quoted (accent of a single ritual term as pronounced by Fulniô speakers at Águas Belas, offered as evidence that Meireles's forms are 'corrupted'). The ~20-item Meireles list is in plain Portuguese orthography with acute accents on some items (ajucá, quaquiquá, pocódó, andaruré, Cancalangó) = wordlist-only data, no statement about Pankararú accent placement. Elsewhere (p. 50) Pinto says the surviving words are 'de estrutura nitidamente cariri'.

sources.citation: Pompeu Sobrinho, Thomaz. 1958. Línguas Tapuias desconhecidas do Nordeste: Alguns vocabulários inéditos. Boletim de Antropologia (Fortaleza) 2(1): 3-19. Vocabulário nº 1 'Brejo dos Padres' (59 items, collected by Carlos Estêvão de Oliveira c. 1940), pp. 10-11; Vocabulário nº 2 (words gathered at Brejo dos Padres but attributed to 'Serra Negra' Indians), pp. 11-12; conventions p. 14.
sources.note: No rule. Orthographic wordlist in which, per the stated convention (p. 14: 'Acento agudo para a tônica'), an acute accent marks the stressed syllable; the Brejo dos Padres items are mostly oxytone (obaí, jinikací, tuká, burúti, kanarí, tarací, umaiatá, tóitú) with some paroxytones (dáka, barkíra, kuriépe, ipá?). The collector himself says the list mixes Tupi, Fulniô and unknown-language words. Nothing said about accent placement as such.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1955. Les langues non-Tupí du Brésil du Nord-Est. In Herbert Baldus (ed.), Anais do XXXI Congresso Internacional de Americanistas (São Paulo, 23-28 de agosto de 1954), vol. II, 1029-1054. São Paulo: Editora Anhembi. (Pankararú passage p. 1041; bibliography pp. 1050-1054.)
sources.note: No phonology at all. The whole treatment of the language is one sentence, p. 1041: 'De leur langue, qui est, elle aussi, une langue isolée, nous ne connaissons que ce qui avait été publié par Pinto (44); les matériaux recueillis par Estevão et mis à la disposition de Nimuendajú furent perdus.' (ref. 44 = Pinto 1938). The paper is a historical survey of NE-Brazil non-Tupi tribes with Kariri-family discussion; it prints no Pankararú word list and no transcription remarks.

sources.citation: Pinto, Estevão. 1952. As mascaras-de-dansa dos Pancararu de Tacaratu (Remanescentes indígenas dos sertões de Pernambuco). Journal de la Société des Américanistes 41(2): 295-304. doi:10.3406/jsa.1952.3745.
sources.note: Nothing. Ten pages read via Persée page views (scanned text, 27 KB): Tacaratu and Brejo-dos-Padres setting, the praiá dance masks (tunã), Gê-vs-Tupi material-culture comparisons after Métraux/Nimuendajú/Nordenskiöld, social organisation. The only language remarks are classificatory: 'Acreditava-se que os Pancararu pertencessem ao grupo cultural-linguístico dos cariris (Kariri, Kiriri, Cariry)' and that by their culture they seem 'remanescentes dos Gê.. já bastantes mesclados com muitos outros tipos filiados a grupos cultural-linguísticos diferentes (tupis, negros e outros)' (pp. 295-296). No…

sources.citation: Estevão [de Oliveira], Carlos. 1942. O ossuário da "Gruta-do-Padre" em Itaparica e algumas notícias sobre remanescentes indígenas do Nordeste. Boletim do Museu Nacional (Rio de Janeiro) XIV-XVII (1938-1941): 151-184, + c. 30 photographic plates.
sources.note: PARTIAL READ: the scan has no text; the 30-page scanned allowance was spent on pp. 33-62, which turned out to be the end of Bastos de Ávila's odontological appendix (p. 184, dated 18 Oct 1937) and photographic plates with captions only. The article text (Boletim pp. 151-183, pp. 1-32) was not scanned. External evidence (Loukotka 1955 p. 1041 citing this paper; Pompeu 1958 calling Estevão's list 'inédito') indicates it prints no vocabulary or phonetic notes; treat as archaeology/ethnography. A reader with eyes on pp. 151-183 could confirm in minutes.

sources.citation: Pinto, Estevão. 1938. Alguns aspétos da cultura artística dos Pancarús de Tacaratú (índios dos sertões de Pernambuco). Revista do Serviço do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional 2: 57-92. Rio de Janeiro: Ministério da Educação e Saúde.
sources.note: No phonology content. Scan has no text; all 26 pages scanned (tesseract por, 300 dpi. kept). Ethnography of material culture, dances (toré, corrida/flechamento do imbú, ajucá, menino do rancho, puxamento do cipó), masks (tunã, 'cinta'), the poró; on language only p. 59/63 (affiliation unclear: Tacaratú and Pindaé are Tupi names; old village name Jiripancó/Jeritacó) and the conclusion p. 92 ('Linguisticamente, as conclusões não se orientam em idêntico sentido, pois são poucos os vocábulos gês que sobreviveram à fusão com os Fulniôs e os tupis'). Ritual terms appear only in running Portuguese t…

sources.citation: Menezes, Hildebrando de. 1935. Os praiás de Tacaratú. Revista do Instituto Arqueológico, Histórico e Geográfico Pernambucano vol. XXXIII (1933-1935), nos. 155-158: 45-48. Recife. (Glottolog: 'de Menezes, Hildebrando 1933-1935', ranked second among its Glottolog's most extensive description candidates, type overview / a wordlist or less.)
sources.note: No language content at all (4 pp. of travel narrative: Serafim, Maria Calú, João Benedito, the praiá dance, photographs); scanned text poor but legible enough to establish this. Not even a wordlist for Pankararú despite Glottolog's 'a wordlist or less' Glottolog's most extensive description typing.

sources.citation: Souza, Fernando J. Carneiro de. 1993. Os Pankararu: aspectos culturais e lingüísticos. Terra Indígena (Araraquara: Centro de Estudos Indígenas, UNESP) 10(66): 20-32.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only title in any bibliography (Fabre 2005; ISA) that claims to treat linguistic aspects of Pankararu; might comment on the wordlists or accentuation, though probably ethnographic.

sources.citation: Pinto, Estevão. 1938. Alguns aspectos da cultura artística dos Pancarús de Tacaratú, índios dos sertões de Pernambuco. Revista do Serviço do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional 2(2): 57-92. (Contains Cildo Meireles's c. 1915 Pankararu ritual vocabulary.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Earliest published set of Pankararu words (ritual terms, toponyms) in accented Portuguese orthography; no rule expected, but completes the primary record.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. n.d. [1930s]. Lista vocabular com 74 itens (Pankarurú). Pasta nº 11, Arquivo da Sala Lingüística, Departamento de Antropologia, Museu Nacional, Rio de Janeiro (cited in Meader 1978, Levantamento bibliográfico, p. 79).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Largest early wordlist of the language, by a careful transcriber who normally marked stress; unpublished manuscript (Museu Nacional archive; status after the 2018 fire unknown).

sources.citation: Crossref works query 'Pankararu lingua' (30 hits, saved); SIL Brazil archive record 16988 for Meader 1978; ISA Povos Indígenas no Brasil page 'Pankararu' (fontes de informação).
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: No linguistic description of Pankararú surfaced: all Crossref hits are ethnography/health/education; ISA's only language-related source is Souza 1993 'Os Pankararu: aspectos culturais e lingüísticos' (Terra Indígena 10/66: 20-32), not online. OLAC, OpenAlex, BASE, Google Scholar, BDTD, SciELO and the UFPE repository were unreachable or could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: das Dores de Oliveira, Maria (2001). A Variação Fonética da Vibrante /r/ na Fala Pankararu: Análise Linguística e Sociolinguística. Maceió: Universidade Federal de Alagoas.
